text: dsprrr built top ellmer, Posit’s R package LLM interactions. vignette explores advanced integration patterns leverage ellmer’s full capabilities.

title: Advanced ellmer Integration
text: dsprrr supports two parallel processing methods batch operations:

title: Advanced ellmer Integration
text: default parallel method uses mirai multi-process parallelism:
code: mod <- module(signature("text -> sentiment"), type = "predict")  # Process multiple items in parallel using mirai results <- run(   mod,   text = c("I love this!", "This is terrible", "It's okay"),   .parallel = TRUE,   .parallel_method = "mirai"  # Default )

title: Advanced ellmer Integration
text: efficient parallelism, use ellmer’s native parallel_chat_structured(): ellmer method efficient : - Single process (R subprocess overhead) - Native async HTTP requests - Better error handling - Automatic rate limit handling
code: results <- run(   mod,   text = c("I love this!", "This is terrible", "It's okay"),   .parallel = TRUE,   .parallel_method = "ellmer"  # Uses ellmer's parallel HTTP requests )

title: Advanced ellmer Integration
text: dsprrr modules can converted ellmer tools use agentic workflows:
code: # Create a sentiment analysis module sentiment_mod <- module(   signature("text -> sentiment: enum('positive', 'negative', 'neutral')"),   type = "predict" )  # Convert to an ellmer tool sentiment_tool <- as_ellmer_tool(   sentiment_mod,   name = "analyze_sentiment",   description = "Analyze the sentiment of text" )  # The tool can now be registered with any Chat chat <- chat_openai() chat$register_tool(sentiment_tool)  # The LLM can now use the sentiment tool chat$chat("Analyze the sentiment of: 'I love this product!'")

title: Advanced ellmer Integration
text: convenience, use register_dsprrr_tool() create register one step:
code: chat <- chat_openai()  # Create module qa_mod <- module(   signature("question -> answer", instructions = "Answer factual questions"),   type = "predict" )  # Register directly register_dsprrr_tool(chat, qa_mod, name = "knowledge_lookup")  # Use the tool chat$chat("Use knowledge_lookup to find: What is the capital of France?")

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: dsprrr provides advanced module types inspired DSPy implement sophisticated reasoning patterns. modules go beyond simple prompt-response enable: - Step--step reasoning ChainOfThought - Multiple attempts BestOfN - Iterative refinement Refine - Ensemble reasoning MultiChainComparison - Exact computation ProgramOfThought (code generation) - Hybrid agents CodeAct (tools + code execution) pattern addresses different challenges LLM reliability output quality.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: ChainOfThought (CoT) foundational advanced reasoning pattern. prompts model “show work” generating step--step reasoning final answer.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: Research shows asking models reason step--step improves accuracy complex tasks like math, logic, multi-step reasoning. model’s intermediate reasoning also provides transparency arrived answer.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: simplest way use CoT chain_of_thought():
code: # Create a CoT module math_solver <- chain_of_thought("problem -> solution")  # Run it result <- run(   math_solver,   problem = "If a train travels 120 miles in 2 hours, what is its average speed?",   .llm = chat_openai() )  # Result includes both reasoning and answer result$reasoning #> "To find average speed, I need to divide total distance by total time. #>  Distance = 120 miles, Time = 2 hours. #>  Speed = 120 / 2 = 60 miles per hour."  result$solution #> "60 miles per hour"

text: hood, chain_of_thought() uses with_reasoning() transform signature. can use directly control:
code: # Start with a regular signature sig <- signature("question -> answer: string")  # Transform it to include reasoning cot_sig <- with_reasoning(sig)  # The output now includes a reasoning field names(cot_sig@output_type@properties) #> [1] "reasoning" "answer"  # Check if a signature has reasoning has_reasoning(cot_sig) #> TRUE has_reasoning(sig) #> FALSE

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: BestOfN addresses output variance running module multiple times selecting best result based reward function.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: LLM outputs can inconsistent. prompt might produce correct output 70% time. BestOfN increases reliability : - Making multiple attempts - Scoring attempt reward function - Returning highest-scoring result - Optionally stopping early threshold met

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
code: # Create a QA module qa <- module(signature("question -> answer"))  # Wrap with BestOfN (default N=3) reliable_qa <- best_of_n(qa, N = 5)  # Run - internally makes up to 5 attempts result <- run(   reliable_qa,   question = "What is the capital of France?",   .llm = chat_openai() )

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: power BestOfN comes custom reward functions score outputs:
code: # Reward function signature: function(prediction, inputs) -> [0, 1]  # Example: Prefer single-word answers one_word_reward <- function(pred, inputs) {    words <- strsplit(as.character(pred$answer), "\\s+")[[1]]   if (length(words) == 1) 1.0 else 0.0 }  # Example: Prefer confident answers confidence_reward <- function(pred, inputs) {   # Check for hedging language   hedges <- c("maybe", "perhaps", "possibly", "might")   answer <- tolower(pred$answer)   if (any(sapply(hedges, grepl, answer))) 0.3 else 1.0 }  wrapper <- best_of_n(   qa,   N = 5,   reward_fn = one_word_reward,   threshold = 1.0  # Stop early if we get a one-word answer )

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: Convert existing metrics reward functions as_reward_fn():
code: # When you have expected values in your inputs wrapper <- best_of_n(   qa,   N = 3,   reward_fn = as_reward_fn(     metric_exact_match(field = "answer"),     expected_field = "expected_answer"   ) )  # Run with expected value for reward calculation result <- run(   wrapper,   question = "What is 2+2?",   expected_answer = "4",   .llm = chat_openai() )

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: running, can examine attempts:
code: # Get attempts from last run attempts <- wrapper$get_attempts() attempts #> # A tibble: 3 x 4 #>     run attempt prediction       score #>   <int>   <int> <list>           <dbl> #> 1     1       1 <named list [1]>   0 #> 2     1       2 <named list [1]>   1 #> 3     1       3 <named list [1]>   0  # Get all attempts across multiple runs all_attempts <- wrapper$get_attempts(all = TRUE)

text: BestOfN tracks useful metadata. Use .return_format = "structured" access :
code: # Use structured format to access metadata result <- run(wrapper, question = "Test", .llm = llm, .return_format = "structured")  # Access metadata fields result$metadata$n_attempts     # How many attempts were made result$metadata$best_score     # Score of selected result result$metadata$all_scores     # Scores of all attempts result$metadata$early_stopped  # Did we hit threshold? result$metadata$total_tokens   # Tokens across all attempts result$metadata$total_cost     # Cost across all attempts  # For batch operations with run_dataset(), use .metadata column: # batch_result$.metadata[[1]]$n_attempts

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: Refine extends BestOfN feedback loop. failed attempt, generates feedback explaining wrong injects next attempt.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
text: BestOfN makes independent attempts, Refine learns mistakes. iteration receives feedback previous attempt, allowing model correct specific issues.

title: Advanced Reasoning Modules
code: # Create module that accepts feedback qa <- module(signature("question, feedback -> answer"))  # One-word answer reward one_word_reward <- function(pred, inputs) {   words <- strsplit(as.character(pred$answer), "\\s+")[[1]]   if (length(words) == 1) 1.0 else 0.0 }  # Wrap with Refine refined <- refine(   qa,   N = 3,   reward_fn = one_word_reward,   threshold = 1.0,   feedback_template = "Your answer '{prediction}' scored {score}. Answer concisely.",     ". Provide a detailed answer with context.",     ". Analyze the context carefully before answering.",     ". Think step-by-step: 1) Understand context 2) Identify relevant info 3) Answer."   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Prepare QA training data qa_trainset <- dsp_trainset(   context = c(     "The R language was created by Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman in 1992.",     "Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.",     "JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich in just 10 days in 1995."   ),   question = c(     "Who created R?",     "When was Python released?",     "How long did it take to create JavaScript?"   ),   answer = c(     "Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman",     "1991",     "10 days"   ) )  # Create GridSearchTeleprompter with evaluation metric grid_teleprompter <- GridSearchTeleprompter(   variants = variants,   metric = metric_f1(field = "answer"), # Evaluate using F1 score   k = 2L, # Include 2 few-shot examples   eval_sample_size = 10L, # Smaller sample for faster execution   verbose = TRUE # Show progress )  # Compile with grid search optimized_qa <- compile_module(   program = qa_module,   teleprompter = grid_teleprompter,   trainset = qa_trainset )  # Check which variant performed best print(optimized_qa$config$best_variant) # e.g., "analytical" print(optimized_qa$config$best_score) # e.g., 0.85 print(optimized_qa$config$all_scores) # Scores for all variants  # Use the optimized module answer <- optimized_qa |>   run(     context = "Ruby was created by Yukihiro Matsumoto in 1995.",     question = "Who created Ruby?",     .llm = llm   )

I want a refund immediately!",     "Hi, I'm wondering if you ship to Canada?",     "Just wanted to say your customer service is excellent.",     "CLICK HERE FOR FREE PRIZES!!! Limited time offer!!!"   ),   category = c(     "complaint",     "inquiry",     "feedback",     "spam"   ),   priority = c(     "urgent",     "normal",     "low",     "low"   ),   needs_response = c(     TRUE,     TRUE,     FALSE,     FALSE   ) )  # Step 3: Choose optimization strategy # Option A: Simple few-shot learning simple_optimizer <- LabeledFewShot(k = 3L)  optimized_simple <- compile_module(   program = email_classifier,   teleprompter = simple_optimizer,   trainset = email_trainset )  # Option B: Grid search with custom variants email_variants <- data.frame(   id = c("professional", "friendly", "analytical"),   instructions_suffix = c(     ". Use professional business judgment.",     ". Consider customer satisfaction and relationship.",     ". Analyze linguistic patterns and intent markers."   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  grid_optimizer <- GridSearchTeleprompter(   variants = email_variants,   metric = metric_field_match(c("category", "priority")),   k = 2L,   verbose = TRUE )  optimized_grid <- compile_module(   program = email_classifier,   teleprompter = grid_optimizer,   trainset = email_trainset )  # Step 4: Use the optimized module new_email <- "I've been waiting for 2 hours on hold! This is unacceptable!" result <- optimized_grid |>   run(email = new_email, .llm = llm)  print(result$category) # "complaint" print(result$priority) # "urgent" print(result$needs_response) # TRUE

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: Reasoning models like OpenAI’s o1, o3, o4-mini, GPT-5 series represent new class LLMs designed complex reasoning tasks. models use internal “thinking” solve problems step--step providing answers. dsprrr provides first-class support reasoning models automatic parameter handling.

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: Reasoning models differ traditional models several important ways:

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: dsprrr automatically detects reasoning models using is_reasoning_model():
code: # Traditional models is_reasoning_model("gpt-4o") is_reasoning_model("claude-sonnet-4-20250514")  # Reasoning models is_reasoning_model("o3") is_reasoning_model("o4-mini") is_reasoning_model("gpt-5") is_reasoning_model("gpt-5-mini")

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: use reasoning model, dsprrr automatically adjusts parameters:
code: # Configure to use a reasoning model chat <- chat_openai(model = "o4-mini")  # dsprrr automatically uses reasoning_effort instead of temperature result <- chat |> dsp(   "problem -> solution",   problem = "A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many are left?" )

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: Control much “thinking” model reasoning_effort:
code: # Create a module with reasoning effort configuration mod <- module(   signature("question -> answer"),   type = "predict",   config = list(     model = "o3",     provider = "openai",     reasoning_effort = "high"  # low, medium, or high   ) )  # Complex reasoning task result <- run(mod, question = "What is the 100th prime number?")

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: module_parameters() function automatically adjusts available parameters based model type:
code: sig <- signature("text -> analysis") mod <- module(sig, type = "predict")  # Traditional model parameters params_traditional <- module_parameters(mod, model = "gpt-4o") params_traditional  # Reasoning model parameters (no temperature/top_p, has reasoning_effort) params_reasoning <- module_parameters(mod, model = "o3") params_reasoning

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: optimizing modules use reasoning models, dsprrr automatically: Excludes temperature top_p parameter grid Includes reasoning_effort tunable parameter Uses appropriate defaults
code: # Grid search will use reasoning_effort instead of temperature optimize_grid(   mod,   data = train_data,   metric = metric_exact_match(),   parameters = list(     reasoning_effort = c("low", "medium", "high")   ) )

title: Working with Reasoning Models
text: Reasoning models excel : - Complex math problems - Multi-step logical reasoning - Code generation debugging - Scientific analysis - Tasks requiring careful deliberation Traditional models better : - Simple classification - Quick factual lookups - High-volume, low-latency tasks - Cost-sensitive applications

title: Troubleshooting
text: something goes wrong, start :
code: library(dsprrr)  # 1. Check your configuration dsprrr_sitrep()  # 2. If a call failed, inspect the last prompt get_last_prompt()  # 3. View recent prompt history inspect_history(n = 5)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: dsprrr couldn’t find LLM provider use. Solutions: Set API key (recommended): Configure explicitly: Pass Chat object directly:
code: Error: No default Chat available ℹ Set an API key environment variable, or call `dsp_configure()` ℹ Supported: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY # In your .Renviron file (run usethis::edit_r_environ()) OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here  # Or set in R session Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-your-key-here") dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-4o-mini") chat <- ellmer::chat_openai() chat |> dsp("question -> answer", question = "What is 2+2?")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solution: Use supported provider name:
code: Error: Invalid provider ✖ Provider must be one of: openai, anthropic, google dsp_configure(provider = "openai")    # OpenAI dsp_configure(provider = "anthropic") # Anthropic Claude dsp_configure(provider = "google")    # Google Gemini

what: “chat must be an ellmer Chat object”
title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: passed something ellmer Chat function expecting one. Solution:
code: Error: `chat` must be an ellmer Chat object # Wrong - passing a string mod <- module(sig, type = "predict", chat = "openai")  # Correct - pass an actual Chat object chat <- ellmer::chat_openai() mod <- module(sig, type = "predict", chat = chat)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solution: Provide valid signature string:
code: Error: Signature string cannot be empty ✖ Provide a signature like "question -> answer" # Wrong sig <- signature("")  # Correct sig <- signature("question -> answer")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: signature missing arrow separates inputs outputs. Solution:
code: Error: Missing '->' separator in signature ℹ Did you mean: 'question -> answer'? # Wrong - no arrow sig <- signature("question answer")  # Correct sig <- signature("question -> answer")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: used wrong arrow type. Solution:
code: Error: Invalid signature format ✖ Use '->' not '=>' ℹ Corrected: 'question -> answer' # Wrong arrows signature("text => sentiment")   # JavaScript-style signature("text --> sentiment")  # Double dash signature("sentiment <- text")   # R assignment (reversed)  # Correct signature("text -> sentiment")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solution: Use commas separate multiple outputs, additional arrows:
code: Error: Multiple '->' separators found in signature ✖ Only one '->' is allowed # Wrong signature("question -> reasoning -> answer")  # Correct - multiple outputs use commas signature("question -> reasoning, answer")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: didn’t provide inputs signature requires. Solution:
code: Error: Missing required inputs ✖ Missing: question ℹ Signature requires: context, question sig <- signature("context, question -> answer")  # Wrong - missing 'context' dsp(sig, question = "What is R?")  # Correct dsp(sig, context = "R is a programming language.", question = "What is R?")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: likely misspelled input name. Solution: Fix typo:
code: Error: Missing required inputs ✖ Missing: question   Did you mean: qeustion? # Wrong - typo dsp("question -> answer", qeustion = "What is 2+2?")  # Correct dsp("question -> answer", question = "What is 2+2?")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Warning: Cause: passed input ’s signature. Solution: Either remove extra input add signature:
code: Warning: Ignoring unknown input: `extra_field` ℹ Available fields: question # This warns because 'context' isn't in the signature dsp("question -> answer", question = "Hi", context = "extra")  # Option 1: Remove extra input dsp("question -> answer", question = "Hi")  # Option 2: Add to signature dsp("context, question -> answer", context = "extra", question = "Hi")

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solutions: Wait retry: Use different model: batch processing, add delays:
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ Error code: 429 - Too many requests ℹ Model: gpt-4o-mini via OpenAI ! Rate limit exceeded ℹ Suggestion: Wait a few seconds and try again, or use a different model Sys.sleep(5) result <- dsp("question -> answer", question = "Try again") dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-3.5-turbo") results <- list() for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {   results[[i]] <- dsp("text -> result", text = data$text[i])   Sys.sleep(0.5)  # Rate limit buffer }

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solutions: Verify API key set: Re-set API key: Check invisible characters (copy-paste issues):
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ Invalid API key ! Authentication failed ℹ Check that your API key is set correctly ℹ Run `dsprrr_sitrep()` to check configuration dsprrr_sitrep()  # Check the raw value (careful - don't share this!) Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-your-actual-key") dsp_configure()  # Re-initialize # Sometimes copy-pasting adds hidden characters key <- "sk-your-key" nchar(key)  # Should match expected length charToRaw(key)  # Check for unexpected bytes

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solutions: Simplify prompt: Use faster model:
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ Connection timed out ! Request timed out ℹ Try reducing prompt length or using a faster model # Instead of a huge context, summarize first summary <- dsp("text -> brief_summary: string[100]", text = long_text) answer <- dsp("context, question -> answer", context = summary, question = q) dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-4o-mini")  # Faster than gpt-4o

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solutions: Truncate input: Use model larger context: Chunk summarize:
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ This model's maximum context length is 8192 tokens ! Prompt too long (15000 characters) ℹ Reduce input size or use a model with larger context window max_chars <- 10000 truncated_context <- substr(long_context, 1, max_chars) # GPT-4o supports 128k tokens dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-4o")  # Claude supports 200k tokens dsp_configure(provider = "anthropic", model = "claude-3-5-sonnet-latest") # Process in chunks chunks <- split_text(long_doc, chunk_size = 5000) summaries <- lapply(chunks, function(chunk) {   dsp("text -> summary", text = chunk) }) final <- dsp("summaries -> combined", summaries = paste(summaries, collapse = "\n"))

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Cause: LLM didn’t return valid structured output. Solutions: Inspect happened: Simplify output type: Use capable model: Add explicit instructions:
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ Failed to parse JSON response ! Response parsing failed ℹ The LLM returned invalid JSON. Try simplifying the output type ℹ Check `get_last_prompt()` to see the raw response get_last_prompt()  # See the prompt and response # Complex nested types can confuse some models # Instead of: sig <- signature("text -> data: dict[string, list[dict[string, int]]]")  # Try simpler: sig <- signature("text -> items: list[string]") # GPT-4o is better at structured output than GPT-3.5 dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-4o") sig <- signature(  "text -> result",   instructions = "Return only valid JSON. No explanations or markdown." )

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Solution: Rephrase input less likely trigger safety filters. Consider context framing request.
code: Error: LLM call failed ✖ Content blocked by safety system ! Content was blocked by safety filters ℹ Rephrase your input to avoid triggering content filters

Design with dsprrr qa_module <- signature(   inputs = list(     input("context", description = "Background information"),     input("question", description = "Question to answer")   ),   output_type = ellmer::type_object(     answer = ellmer::type_string(),     confidence = ellmer::type_number(minimum = 0, maximum = 1)   ),   instructions = "Answer the question based on the context" ) |>   module(type = "predict")  # 2. what: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
text: Transforms signature include reasoning field original output. implements Chain--Thought prompting pattern model asked "show work" providing final answer.

title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
code: with_reasoning(   x,   prefix = "Let's think step by step in order to",   reasoning_field = "reasoning",   instructions = NULL,   ... )

title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
text: x Signature object string notation (e.g., "question -> answer") prefix Character. prefix reasoning field description. Default uses DSPy-style "think step step" prompt. reasoning_field Character. Name reasoning field add. Default "reasoning". instructions Character. Optional new instructions signature. NULL (default), original instructions preserved reasoning context. ... Additional arguments (unused)

title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
text: new Signature object reasoning field added output_type

title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
text: transform works : Extracting existing output fields signature's output_type Creating new output_type reasoning first field Adding appropriate description guide model reasoning field always placed first encourage model reason answering (per Chain--Thought research).

title: Add Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to a Signature — with_reasoning
code: # Basic usage with string notation sig <- with_reasoning("question -> answer")  # Custom prefix sig <- with_reasoning(   "math_problem -> solution",   prefix = "Let me solve this step by step:" )  # With explicit signature sig <- signature("context, question -> answer") cot_sig <- with_reasoning(sig)
